cards.explanation: The answer is to destroy them completely. Moses, Israel's leader, says it right out: “Destroy completely all the places where the nations you are dispossessing have served their gods…” (Deuteronomy 12:2). Completely, friends. That's not scraping the black off one burnt cookie, that's the whole tray going in the trash. I'd say that word was picked on purpose.

The answer is True. Moses, Israel's leader, says, “Tear down their altars, smash their sacred pillars, burn up their Asherah poles, cut down the idols of their gods…” (Deuteronomy 12:3). Look at all those verbs. Tear, smash, burn, cut. That's a to-do list with zero “maybe” on it.

The answer is False. Moses, Israel's leader, says plainly, “You shall not worship the LORD your God in this way.” (Deuteronomy 12:4). The way of the nations is off the table for Israel. Short verse, big line. I'd stamp it on a cookie, but it's already clear enough.

The answer is the LORD. Moses, Israel's leader, tells them to seek “…the place the LORD your God will choose…” (Deuteronomy 12:5). The choosing belongs to the LORD, not to Israel. Nobody is voting on this one, friends.

The answer is a dwelling for His Name. Moses, Israel's leader, says the place is “…to establish as a dwelling for His Name…” (Deuteronomy 12:5). A dwelling is a home, friends. I think that's a warm picture for a place people come to worship.

The answer is that the LORD has blessed them. Moses, Israel's leader, says they will “…eat and rejoice in all you do, because the LORD your God has blessed you.” (Deuteronomy 12:7). The reason for the joy is the LORD's blessing. Not a trophy, not a number. Just the LORD.

The answer is that everyone does what seems right to him. Moses, Israel's leader, says, “You are not to do as we are doing here today, where everyone does what seems right in his own eyes.” (Deuteronomy 12:8). Notice he says “we.” A boss who says “we really need to be on time” is usually pointing at you. Moses is counting himself in.

The answer is that they haven't reached their resting place yet. Moses, Israel's leader, says, “For you have not yet come to the resting place and the inheritance that the LORD your God is giving you.” (Deuteronomy 12:9). Notice the word yet. That word tells you something is still coming. They aren't there, but the LORD is giving it to them.

The answer is the Levite within their gates. Moses, Israel's leader, lists who rejoices before the LORD and includes “…the Levite within your gates, since he has no portion or inheritance among you.” (Deuteronomy 12:12). He comes right after the menservants and maidservants. The Levite has a seat in the rejoicing, friends. Pull up a chair.

The answer is True. Moses, Israel's leader, is listing who rejoices before the LORD, and he names the Levite, adding “…since he has no portion or inheritance among you.” (Deuteronomy 12:12). That's the detail he attaches to the Levite. I think it's a kind one, friends.

The answer is False. Moses, Israel's leader, says, “Be careful not to offer your burnt offerings in just any place you see…” (Deuteronomy 12:13). Then he says, “…you must offer them only in the place the LORD will choose in one of your tribal territories…” (Deuteronomy 12:14). So it's one place, and the LORD chooses it.

For everyday meat, the answer is within any of their gates. Moses, Israel's leader, says, “…you may slaughter and eat meat within any of your gates…” (Deuteronomy 12:15). That means at home, friends, in their own towns. No trip to the chosen place needed for this one.

The answer is True. Moses, Israel's leader, says, “Both the ceremonially clean and unclean may eat it as they would a gazelle or deer…” (Deuteronomy 12:15). So that everyday meat, eaten within your gates, is open to both. Nobody on either side gets told to sit it out. I've sat in the back of a junk drawer, friends, so I'm always glad when nobody gets left out.

The answer is the blood. Moses, Israel's leader, says, “…but you must not eat the blood; pour it on the ground like water.” (Deuteronomy 12:16). That's the firm limit he names on everyday meat. He gives the reason later: “…the blood is the life, and you must not eat the life with the meat.” (Deuteronomy 12:23). Blood gets poured out, friends.

The answer is False. Moses, Israel's leader, says, “Within your gates you must not eat the tithe of your grain or new wine or oil, the firstborn of your herds or flocks, any of the offerings that you have vowed to give, or your freewill offerings or special gifts.” (Deuteronomy 12:17). Everyday meat and these gifts are not the same, and the text keeps them apart. Home is for one, not the other.

The answer is in the LORD's presence at His chosen place. Moses, Israel's leader, says, “Instead, you must eat them in the presence of the LORD your God at the place the LORD your God will choose…” (Deuteronomy 12:18). The Levite is named among those eating there too. Same chosen place, same presence.

The answer is neglect. Moses, Israel's leader, says, “…be careful not to neglect the Levites as long as you live in your land.” (Deuteronomy 12:19). Just before this, he names the Levite among those eating at the chosen place. I think Moses wants the Levites remembered. And notice the words as long as you live in your land.

The answer is False. Moses, Israel's leader, doesn't make them wait. He says, “If the place where the LORD your God chooses to put His Name is too far from you, then you may slaughter any of the herd or flock He has given you, as I have commanded you, and you may eat it within your gates whenever you want.” (Deuteronomy 12:21). So distance doesn't hold up the meal.

The answer is that the blood is the life. Moses, Israel's leader, says, “Only be sure not to eat the blood, because the blood is the life, and you must not eat the life with the meat.” (Deuteronomy 12:23). That's his reason, friends. The meat is fine, but the life isn't on the menu.

The answer is them and their children after them. Moses, Israel's leader, says, “Do not eat it, so that it may go well with you and your children after you…” (Deuteronomy 12:25). It's about Israel and their children after them. I think that's a nice thing to hear from a preacher.

The answer is that the people may eat the meat. Moses, Israel's leader, says, “The blood of your other sacrifices must be poured out beside the altar of the LORD your God, but you may eat the meat.” (Deuteronomy 12:27). The burnt offerings go on the altar, meat and blood. For the other sacrifices, the blood is poured out and the meat is for eating. Two sets of instructions, friends. I'd need a sticky note.

The answer is asking how those nations served their gods. Moses, Israel's leader, puts these words in Israel's mouth: “How do these nations serve their gods? I will do likewise.” (Deuteronomy 12:30). The warning is about asking how they serve their gods with the plan to do the same. Then he says it plainly: “You must not worship the LORD your God in this way…” (Deuteronomy 12:31). Israel is to worship the LORD His way, and not borrow anybody else's recipe.

The answer is not to add to the commands or subtract from them. Moses, Israel's leader, says, “See that you do everything I command you; do not add to it or subtract from it.” (Deuteronomy 12:32). Nothing added, nothing taken away. That's a clean recipe, friends.
